Wood documentation

Get up and running.

Install once. Keep the controls you need close to your next attempt.

Getting startedTime WarpMod developmentUninstallingTroubleshooting

Install Wood

  1. Install and launch TUNG through Steam at least once.
  2. Download WoodSetup.exe. Close TUNG and any Wood launcher.
  3. Exit Steam using Steam → Exit if you want setup to configure launch options.
  4. Run the installer. Confirm the detected TUNG folder, or use Browse to select it.
  5. Leave Configure Steam checked for automatic integration. Untick it if you use another launch wrapper.
  6. Click Install Wood. Reopen Steam and launch TUNG.
  7. Press F10 or click the native Mods button when the game is ready.
No separate Python or UE4SS download is needed. Setup includes both the launcher and the pinned runtime.

Use Time Warp

Set a speed between 0.05× and 4× with the slider or preset buttons. The launcher shows the speed confirmed by the engine.

KeyAction
F10Open or close the native mod menu
F6Halve world speed
F7Reset to 1×
F8Double world speed
EscapeClose the mod menu

Disable Time Warp to restore 1× while retaining your selected speed. Reset speed on world change returns to normal speed when moving to another world. Settings persist between launches.

Use speed changes for practice or categories that permit tools. Check your category’s rules before recording a submitted run; Wood does not certify leaderboard eligibility.

Manage mods

Open WoodLauncher.exe from your TUNG folder. Search the mod library and enable or disable native mods. Mod selection changes take effect on the next launch. Third-party native extensions belong in NativeMods/<mod-id>/.

Legacy Python overlay mods remain on disk and are listed for reference. The native runtime does not execute them.

Uninstall Wood

  1. Close TUNG and Wood. Exit Steam if setup configured launch options.
  2. Open Windows Settings → Apps → Installed apps → Wood for TUNG → Uninstall, or run WoodUninstall.exe in the TUNG folder.
  3. Click Uninstall Wood. Reopen Steam when finished.

Uninstall restores owned files from backups and removes unchanged files installed by Wood. Personal settings, custom mods, and backups remain. Files you edited after installation are preserved and reported. Steam launch options are restored only if they still match Wood’s installed value.

Troubleshooting

Setup asks me to close Steam.

Steam can overwrite local configuration while running. Use Steam → Exit, complete setup, then reopen Steam. Untick Steam integration to install without changing Steam settings.

TUNG was not detected.

Browse to the folder containing TUNG.exe and the TUNG subfolder. Install and launch the game through Steam once first.

F10 does not open the menu.

Wait for the world to initialize. Check TUNG/Binaries/Win64/ue4ss/UE4SS.log and .wood/status.json. Close the game and rerun setup if runtime files are missing.

The launcher says runtime offline.

The connection appears when TUNG is running and Wood has initialized. A previous session’s status is deliberately treated as offline. Launcher errors are logged in .wood/launcher.log.

I already use another loader or Steam wrapper.

Keep your current Steam wrapper by unticking Steam integration. Setup stops if an incompatible dwmapi.dll proxy is present. Existing UE4SS installations and unrelated mods are preserved.
